findings.title: Certain requirements of State law and recognized best practices were not incorporated into Washington County Public Schools’ (WCPS) procurement policies and were not consistently used when participating in intergovernmental cooperative purchasing agreements.
findings.description: WCPS did not incorporate statutory requirements or best practices into procurement policies for ICPAs. They used the ICPA method for 82 procurements totaling approximately $94.2 million but lacked written assessments justifying cost benefits or administrative efficiencies. Testing of 5 ICPAs totaling approximately $8.3 million disclosed missing best practices such as analyzing costs of competitive solicitations.
findings.recommendation: WCPS should incorporate the aforementioned statutory requirements and other identified and acknowledged best practices into its procurement policies and ensure that the performance of the requirements and best practices are documented when evaluating and participating in ICPAs.

findings.title: WCPS published contract awards on its website instead of on eMaryland Marketplace Advantage as required by State procurement law.
findings.description: WCPS did not publish contract awards on eMMA as required by State law for contracts $50,000 or more. From July 1, 2022 to February 20, 2024, WCPS published 78 contract awards valued at or over $50,000 totaling $57.3 million on its website instead of eMMA.

dollar_amounts.context: aggregate contract awards not published on eMMA

findings.recommendation: WCPS should comply with State procurement law by publishing contract awards on eMMA as required.

findings.title: WCPS did not competitively procure a $3.6 million nursing services contract that has been awarded annually to the same vendor since 2013, and did not obtain available supporting documentation to ensure that related billings were proper.
findings.description: WCPS awarded a one-year $3.6 million nursing contract to the incumbent without competitive bids in August 2022 (similar awards made since 2013). WCPS did not obtain detailed staff timesheets or assignment reports to validate vendor billings for invoices totaling approximately $454,000 and $390,000.
findings.recommendation: WCPS should ensure that contracts are competitively procured and awarded; use available supporting documentation (such as timesheets and staff assignment reports) to validate the propriety of vendor billings.

findings.title: WCPS did not independently review payroll adjustments for propriety.
findings.description: WCPS did not independently review payroll adjustments for propriety. Two employees calculated and entered adjustments totaling approximately $1.2 million in fiscal year 2023 without independent supervisory review or approval. Testing of 10 leave payout adjustments valued at approximately $673,000 disclosed no inappropriate transactions.
findings.recommendation: WCPS should perform a documented independent supervisory review of payroll adjustments to ensure that they are appropriate and properly supported.

findings.title: WCPS did not adequately monitor the performance of its third-party administrator that provided medical healthcare and pharmacy claims processing services.
findings.description: WCPS did not adequately monitor TPA performance. Payments to the TPA totaled approximately $1.1 million in fiscal year 2023. WCPS did not obtain claim data for supporting amounts billed; last audit was FY 2018 (recoveries $19,477). Pharmacy rebates totaled $7.3 million during fiscal year 2023.
findings.recommendation: WCPS should establish procedures to verify the propriety of TPA claim billings; conduct claims audits; obtain and use detailed claim payment data for stop-loss limit; conduct pharmacy TPA audits; establish a process to independently verify TPA compliance with performance measures.

findings.title: WCPS did not have memorandums of agreement with its affiliated foundations to address each entity’s roles and responsibilities.
findings.description: WCPS did not have MOAs with BISFAF and WCPSEF. BISFAF revenues/expenditures/assets FY2023 were $274,000/$242,000/$2.1 million. WCPSEF reported revenues/expenditures/assets FY2023 were $111,000/$128,000/$69,000.
findings.recommendation: WCPS should enter into MOAs with affiliated foundations detailing roles and responsibilities for each entity in critical areas such as conflicts of interest, collection and safeguarding funds, and procurement policies.

extraction.agency_response_summary: WCPS agreed to all recommendations and provided corrective action plans with estimated completion dates ranging from January 2025 to September 2025.
